determinism.canonicalization: UTF-8 canonical JSON uses NFC strings, sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, no floats, no duplicate keys, and exactly one trailing newline
determinism.graph: module paths, resolved imports, roots, source users, entry closures, dynamic calls, effects, symbols, surfaces, and checks use stable lexical ordering and deduplicate
determinism.identity: inventory_sha256 covers canonical inventory bytes with only itself replaced by 64 zeroes; report_sha256 covers the canonical report with only itself replaced by 64 zeroes
determinism.platform: analysis uses Python AST syntax and declared root classes rather than importing modules, querying installed packages, resolving executable paths, reading machine identity, or depending on checkout location
determinism.replay: the same repository bytes yield byte-identical reports under dependency-minimal and full-jsonschema interpreters and in a relocated checkout

effects.filesystem: library validation reads repository-owned contract, schema, fixture, inventory, report, pyproject, and Python source bytes only; CLI report generation atomically replaces one explicit repository-relative report path
effects.mutation: no caller-owned object is retained or mutated and returned report values are newly allocated
effects.process: none during library validation; isolated-subprocess reproducibility is exercised only by the external test command
effects.solver: none and no mathhead, Z3, SymPy, PySAT, mpmath, MCP, or Lean module is imported or executed

ensures: Validation returns one canonical deterministic report covering the complete source-module inventory, static import graph, import-root usage, entry-point transitive closures, dynamic import calls, effect-bearing imports, authority-bearing symbols, inventory identities, and all semantic checks.

New, missing, duplicate, stale, cyclic, unresolved, or reclassified modules, entry points, import roots, surfaces, roles, authority tiers, trusted bytes, migration owners, or report fields fail closed rather than being silently accepted.

Every third-party solver, CAS, numerical backend, transport, dynamic import, subprocess, multiprocessing, filesystem, environment, parser, serializer, hashing, arithmetic, checker, runtime, and proof-assistant boundary has exactly one explicit current policy and migration disposition.

Producer, transport, orchestration, parsing, serialization, hashing, approximate arithmetic, environment, and effect boundaries cannot acquire checker attestation or external proof-assistant authority through inventory validity.

Current checker claims distinguish stdlib certificate checking, two RUP or DRUP implementations, the discovery LCF-style kernel, and solver-backed verification; duplicate or hidden trusted primitives remain visible until their assigned P3 migration closes them.

The future dependency-minimal checker target has closed import allow and deny lists, exact allowed primitives, forbidden effects and capabilities, zero third-party, dynamic-import, process, filesystem, network, clock, random, and environment authority, and a finite source and import budget.

Dependency-minimal and full-jsonschema validation produce identical report bytes, and a relocated repository copy reproduces those bytes without importing mathhead runtime modules or third-party packages.

Writing a report is explicit and atomic at the CLI boundary; library validation is read-only and neither executes imports nor starts solvers, subprocesses, workers, network clients, or proof assistants.

epistemics.checker_attestation: inventory validity may describe checker boundaries but never establishes that a proof, certificate, theorem, solver, arithmetic primitive, Python runtime, or external proof assistant is sound
epistemics.external_proof_assistant: Lean export remains pending with no authority until a separately pinned toolchain produces an independently bound successful replay artifact
epistemics.invalid: any structural, semantic, graph, identity, byte, classification, budget, or reproducibility failure yields no usable trust inventory
epistemics.producer_report: Z3, SymPy, PySAT, mpmath, nauty, search, transport, and orchestration outputs remain producer or numerical reports unless separately checked
epistemics.valid: the declared trusted-computing-base description exactly matches the statically observable repository boundary and its frozen report; this is governance evidence, not mathematical truth

invariants: The normative schema is docs/trust/trust-base-v1.schema.json=99c3024ffc5f2de636d2a61ed9c01a9396aa51c1f54b09fe14e6dde7d6816f3d; it is closed Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema and both dependency-minimal structural checks and the optional standard meta-validator accept it.

Contract, schema, MH-027 report, MH-028 manifest, bundle, trusted-byte, source, and report paths are exact-case repository-relative regular files that cannot escape the repository root or traverse symlinks outside it.

IDs, paths, targets, import roots, source paths, surface references, migration references, allowlists, denylists, primitives, capabilities, risks, failures, and controls are unique, sorted where order is nonsemantic, and all references resolve exactly once.

The five authority tiers are none, producer_report, solver_verdict, checker_attestation, and external_proof_assistant in that order; only the last three may represent mathematical authority and each retains its distinct trust dependency.

Parser, canonicalizer, identity, approximate arithmetic, producer, orchestrator, transport, runtime, and effect roles cannot grant checker or proof-assistant authority; checker and proof-assistant roles are separately owned.

Static imports are collected from every AST scope without importing modules; relative imports resolve against the source module, every internal target exists, and every external root equals the exact declared root inventory.
Console scripts match pyproject.toml exactly, public checker and proof-kernel targets exist exactly once, and every entry closure contains only declared internal modules and import roots.

Dynamic import_module and __import__ calls, subprocess, multiprocessing, filesystem, environment, random, clock, network-facing transport, solver, CAS, and numerical roots are recorded in the report and mapped to explicit non-checker policies.

The target checker allowlist and denylist are disjoint; z3, sympy, pysat, mpmath, mcp, subprocess, multiprocessing, importlib, os, pathlib, random, shutil, sys, and time are denied, and every effect or non-exact capability is explicitly forbidden.

Migration order contains exactly MH-031 through MH-037, starts from MH-030, is acyclic, covers every current non-final surface, and does not claim that a future owner or authority exists before its assigned task completes.

The generated report has one stable schema and identity, contains no timestamps, absolute paths, environment values, package versions, host facts, unordered sets, or source content, and report comparison is byte exact.
raises: TrustBaseValidationError with kind schema for invalid JSON, duplicate keys, unknown or missing fields, wrong scalar or collection types, malformed IDs, paths, targets, hashes, tasks, enums, or noncanonical bytes.

TrustBaseValidationError with kind contract, foundation, source, import, entry-point, surface, authority, primitive, effect, migration, identity, report, path, or budget for the corresponding failed invariant.
OSError and UnicodeError are translated to a classified fail-closed validation error; MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit are never converted into a valid inventory or ordinary report.
requires: The repository contains canonical docs/trust/trust-base-v1.json governed by docs/trust/trust-base-v1.schema.json=99c3024ffc5f2de636d2a61ed9c01a9396aa51c1f54b09fe14e6dde7d6816f3d and unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

The inventory binds accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca and MH-C-TRUST-BASE-001 bytes, the MH-027 conformance report, and the MH-028 reference bundle=4132b29b69600f8ff48477515853f66bb748c7337735c00db8e634987f70ddca.
Source scope is exactly every Python file below src/mathhead with no exclusions, and every supported console, public-checker, and proof-kernel entry point is declared by exact target.
Every imported non-mathhead root is declared once with language, standard-library, or third-party kind, one owning trust surface, one policy, and a nonempty rationale.

Every surface declares exact owner, role, current and target authority, state, required status, sources, imports, trusted primitives and bytes, attacks, failures, controls, and one MH-030 through MH-037 migration owner.
